title: Enterprise ask translation to solution hypotheses and rapid-scope playbook
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Sales and CS bring high-variance enterprise asks that are hard to compare and scope quickly. We need a lightweight, consistent way to convert customer requests into 1-page solution hypotheses (what we would build, why, constraints, and rough level-of-effort range) that sales/CS can use for near-term commercial conversations and PM/ENG prioritization.

Goal: Deliver a rapid-scope playbook + one-pager template and a four-factor rubric (value, risk/regulatory, engineering effort, time-to-value) so that within one business day a Solutions Engineer or PM can produce a scoping hypothesis that is sufficient for commercial sizing and initial roadmap decisions.

Scope: This ticket covers template creation, rubric calibration using 12 recent enterprise asks, a short enablement doc for sales/CS/SEs, and a lightweight QA step with two customer examples (FinCo and MedWork). It does NOT cover implementation backlog tracking or automated intake UI changes (those will be separate tickets).

Deliverables: 1) One-page solution hypothesis template (Markdown + fillable Google Doc), 2) Rubric with worked examples and scoring guidance, 3) Enablement slide deck and 30-minute training script, 4) Handful of annotated examples from real customer requests, 5) Short PRD stub for follow-up automation work.
acceptance_criteria: One-page solution hypothesis template produced and stored in Drive
Four-factor rubric defined with clear scoring bands and example scores for 12 historical asks
At least two annotated customer examples (FinCo, MedWork) validated by sales leads
Enablement deck created and 30-minute training run with Sales Ops (attendance recorded)
Rubric reviewed and approved by one PM, one SE, and one engineering tech lead (explicit sign-off in comments)
comments: 2026-02-25 | Aisha Patel: Kickoff — pulled 12 enterprise asks from Sales queue for calibration. Initial hypothesis: customers cluster into three solution archetypes (data-connectors + private inference, fine-tuning/embedding pipelines, and routing/business-logic orchestration). Planning to test rubric against those archetypes.

2026-02-27 | Marco Lin: Drafted initial one-pager template. Key trade-off: how prescriptive should the implementation section be? Proposal: keep high-level options (hosted API, dedicated, private) and associate typical LOE bands instead of committing to exact implementation steps. This keeps the template useful across accounts.

2026-03-01 | Jordan Rivera (Solutions Eng): Reviewed sample for FinCo. Feedback: emphasize data residency/regulatory risk in scoring; suggested adding an explicit 'third-party data transfer' flag. Added to rubric as a gating multiplier.

2026-03-02 | Priya Desai (Sales Lead): Confirmed enablement timeline; asked for a version of the template that can be created from a Slack thread or email in under 20 minutes. Action: produce a TL;DR variant and a filled example from last quarter (MedWork).

2026-03-03 | Elena Gomez (Engineering TL): Concern about LOE variance for 'private on-prem' items; recommended LOE bands include hardware procurement and security review windows. Updated LOE band guidance and added example cadence (3-6 months vs 6-12 months).

2026-03-04 | Marco Lin: Uploaded draft docs to Drive and opened PRD stub: https://drive.redwood.ai/enterprise-playbooks/pm-514271-draft and PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/pm-docs/pull/214. Requesting PM/SE/Eng sign-off by 2026-03-08.

2026-03-05 | Aisha Patel: Ran training dry-run with Sales Ops; captured questions around refund/credit policy for missed SLAs in dedicated offers — logged as follow-up and dependency on legal/commercial (PM-514275).
notes: Decision: will not automate scoring yet; first 6 weeks operate manually to gather signal and calibrate numeric thresholds.

Trade-off: faster scoping favors conservative LOE bands which may overestimate cost; mitigation: add a 'fast-track' checkbox for deals that require tighter estimates and route to Solutions Eng for deeper analysis.
Next steps: calibrate rubric with two additional customers (energy vertical) and onboard Sales Ops to create at least 10 hypothesis docs in March for signal collection.
